h: Fly Smart, Then Explore Greenwich Peninsula
p: The briefing tells you how to fly, but here's the cheat sheet: relax, chin up, hips forward, arms soft. Fight the air and it fights back. Let it hold you and suddenly you're floating. Your instructor will do the rest, steering you round the tunnel and nudging you into the right shape with hand signals.

Practical prep makes a difference here. Leave jewellery, watches and anything in your pockets in a locker, wear lace-up trainers and comfortable clothes, and tie back long hair. If you've got any old injuries, especially shoulders or backs, mention them at check-in. On concert nights, the whole O2 gets packed, so allow extra time to get through the crowds.

After your flight, there's more to see without going far. The Uber Boat by Thames Clippers river bus calls at North Greenwich Pier, giving you a scenic ride along the Thames towards Greenwich, Canary Wharf and central London. Over in Greenwich itself, the National Maritime Museum is free and full of maritime treasures, and the Painted Hall at the Old Royal Naval College is a jaw-dropper.

If the weather is kind, grab an ice cream and enjoy the riverside path around the peninsula, which has great views across to Canary Wharf. There are plenty of places to eat around The O2, so you won't go hungry after all that flying.
